channel.title: Breaking Defense – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Breaking Defense – Bias and Credibility (breakingdefense.com)

item.title: Space Force anticipates first Kronos C2 contracts in April - Breaking Defense
item.description: While Kronos is moving forward, the other major part of the C2 upgrade, ATLAS, has not reached full viability, according to the most recent report by DOT&amp;E.

item.title: Swiss Destinus, Shield AI wrap European drone autonomy test campaign - Breaking Defense
item.description: Despite the absence of customers, the companies are hoping that the demonstration could tempt European air forces looking for cUAS solutions that can reduce reliance on crewed aircraft.

item.title: General Dynamics-led team unveils self-driving truck with microwave counter-drone tech - Breaking Defense
item.description: The Leonidas Autonomous Ground Vehicle consists of a commercial Ford F600 model truck tricked out with Kodiak’s autonomous driving software and Eprius’ high-power microwave (HPM) c-UAS platform.

item.title: What new weapons could a supplemental buy, plus news on the Army's C5ISR plans - Breaking Defense
item.description: Rep. Rob Wittman, plus Pentagon officials Jules Hurst and Joseph Welch, all make an appearance on the Break Out this week.

item.title: Air Force seeks industry feedback to 'benchmark' progress of Northrop missile - Breaking Defense
item.description: The Air Force told Breaking Defense the service may consider producing another missile similar to Northrop Grumman’s Stand-in Attack Weapon “if industry has solid options for delivering munitions faster and cheaper.”

item.title: Hormuz disruption will change trade — and defense — at other chokepoints - Breaking Defense
item.description: Disruption at the Strait of Hormuz will set off a chain reaction of pressure through the global shipping network, requiring international defense efforts, writes US Navy Supply Corps Capt. Michael Kidd.

item.title: Industry bullish on DoC draft license process for novel space activities - Breaking Defense
item.description: The Office of Space Commerce certification process would be voluntary for industry, due to the fact that congressional authorization would be required for the imposition of any new regulations.

item.title: Army’s enterprise contracting vehicles likely to speed procurement but not without risk - Breaking Defense
item.description: An expert and former defense officials told Breaking Defense that the service’s push to award high ceiling, prolonged contracts could speed up acquisition processes but ultimately only time will determine their effectiveness.

item.title: ST Engineering to serve as subcontractor for Kuwaiti navy vessels deal - Breaking Defense
item.description: The contract is valued at 600 million Singapore dollars (467.6 million USD).

item.title: Edgewing receives first GCAP next-gen fighter international contract to boost design activities - Breaking Defense
item.description: The new funding invests in "key design and engineering activities and enables the trilateral partnership to build momentum and accelerate pace of delivery."

item.title: A year after ‘Liberation Day,’ impact of Trump tariffs on defense industry remains muted - Breaking Defense
item.description: Experts and former defense officials said exemptions to the tariffs imposed by the Trump administration have somewhat blunted the financial impact on the defense industrial base.

item.title: Space Force plans to establish HQ staff group as surrogate Futures Command - Breaking Defense
item.description: CSO Gen. Chance Saltzman has signed a memo, obtained by Breaking Defense, initiating the creation of SF/S9 to coordinate future force planning. However, the change has yet to be approved by Air Force Secretary Troy Meink.

item.title: Iran conflict could open door for new players in Gulf defense market - Breaking Defense
item.description: As Gulf countries reassess defense needs after the Iran conflict, new entrants may find a windfall, writes Alek Jovovic of CSIS.

item.title: Hegseth fires Army's top officer, Gen. Randy George - Breaking Defense
item.description: A Defense Department official confirmed a report that George has been asked to step down by Hegseth.

item.title: Trump to propose $1.5 trillion defense budget, banking on $350 billion from reconciliation - Breaking Defense
item.description: The fiscal 2027 request, to be formally revealed Friday, marks the first time that base budget defense spending has hit the $1 trillion mark, with reconciliation funds on top of that.
